text:
ryan: Quick hit — ran a comparison between FlashAttention-v2, our fused-attn kernel, and the paged-attn fallback. Seeing a ~18% regression for fused-attn at seq_len=1024 when batch_size >= 12. Not sure if it's kernel selection or KV layout.

ingrid: Can you paste the bench command + machine? A100 or H100? and dtype?

ryan: A100-40GB, fp16. Command was: `python bench_attention.py --model gpt2-xl --seq 1024 --batch 16 --kernels flash,fused,paged --kv-layout interleaved` — full output attached (trimmed):
```
flash:  8.9 ms/token
fused: 10.5 ms/token  <-- regression
paged:  11.2 ms/token
```

sam: Interesting. Did the fused path change recently in the kernel selector? I remember a change that prefers 128B alignment for blocks.

marie: Also check strides for KV tensors. If interleaved layout causes non-coalesced stores for the fused kernel's write pattern, that would blow up throughput.

alex: Repro tip: run small microbench with `--batch 1,4,8,12,16` and log peak SM utilization + L2 bw. If fused hits lower SM utilization while flash stays high => memory pattern issue.

ryan: I ran microbench quick. For batch=8 fused SM=92%, batch=16 fused SM=63%. Flash stayed ~90% in both. L2 bw for fused jumped 30% at batch=16.

ingrid: L2 increasing + SM dropping smells like serialization on memory ops. Stride/alignment mismatch. What is our interleaved layout stride? IIRC we interleave kv: [batch, head, seq, d_k] contiguous by head then seq.

marie: Right, layout = B, H, S, Dk with stride S*Dk for head. If fused expects head-major contiguous Dk then it might do scattered writes across sequences.

ryan: I quickly tried switching KV to "separate" (i.e., store K and V per-head contiguous: [B, S, H, Dk]) and reran fused.
```
fused (separate): 9.6 ms/token  (was 10.5)
flash (separate): 8.8 ms/token
paged (separate): 11.0 ms/token
```
So separate layout recovered ~9% for fused.

alex: That's a smoking gun. We should update kernel selector to prefer fused+separate for batch >= 12 on A100 for seq>=1024.

sam: Before we change selector, verify dtype alignment: are we using packed fp16 (2 bytes) or bf16? On A100 fp16 aligned to 256B blocks gives best coalescing. If our allocator pads to 128B only, that could break fused assumptions.

ingrid: Allocator pads to 128B currently. PR #4128 had target to reduce memory but removed 256B padding. I've opened a quick PR to add 256B pad optional per-kv-buffer.

marie: Also consider page size for paged-attn. If paged granularity is 512 tokens and we fetch pages with strided accesses, interleaved hurts more. We might want to transpose when paged mode is enabled.

ryan: Logged a perf regression issue: `perf/ATTN-652` with attached microbench traces. cc @ci-bench-bot to run the nightly matrix with both layouts and kernel combos.

ci-bench-bot: queued bench matrix: kernels=[flash,fused,paged], layouts=[interleaved,separate], seq=[512,1024,2048], batch=[4,8,12,16] on A100. ETA ~4h :hourglass:

alex: When the CI runs finish, please capture Nsight compute export for a few rows. Specifically look at `sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_elapsed`, `lts__t_sectors_hit`, and `sm__inst_executed`. That will tell us if tensor core utilization dropped.

sam: One more note — fused kernel recently added a reduction step that uses 32-bit accumulators when Dk > 128. That increases register pressure and may change tiling decisions. Could interact badly with layout.

ingrid: Good call. If fused switches tiling at Dk>128 and layout causes stride jumps, the register spill could force more global memory traffic.

ryan: Plan: 1) CI matrix (ci-bench-bot) 2) repro single-run with Nsight on batch=16 seq=1024 with both layouts 3) try padding allocator to 256B 4) if confirmed, update selector to prefer separate+fused for those combos and add fallback to flash.

marie: Also add a Canary test that runs batch=12/16 seq=1024 for each kernel variant to catch regressions in PRs.

ryan: I'll open the kernel-selector PR after CI. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: Nice investigative work. If we confirm layout is the root cause we should document layout expectations in the kernel API (e.g., required strides, alignment) so future devs don't accidentally change allocators.

ci-bench-bot: results uploaded: https://ci.redwood/inference/bench/ATTN-652 (summary CSV + nsight zips)

ryan: I downloaded one trace — attaching short snippet of the Nsight summary:
```
configuration: A100 fp16 batch=16 seq=1024 layout=interleaved kernel=fused
sm__inst_executed: 8.2e9
sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_elapsed: 1.2e8
lts__t_sectors_hit_ratio: 0.42
```

ryan: With separate layout:
```
sm__inst_executed: 1.1e10
sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_elapsed: 1.05e8
lts__t_sectors_hit_ratio: 0.78
```

marie: Perfect. LTS hit ratio jump from .42 to .78 explains the perf delta. Let's proceed with the selector change + allocator pad flag.

sam: I'll add a small unit test that verifies kernel selection table yields fused+separate for the tuned combos.

ingrid: And I'll add docs to eng-runtime/README about KV layout expectations.

ryan: Filing follow-ups: ATT-652 (investigation), ATT-653 (selector PR), ATT-654 (allocator pad opt), ATT-655 (canary test). Closing for now.
